MARKET.head: Moldova pitches indigenous grape varieties to Chinese buyers at ProWine Shanghai
MARKET.summ: With 23 wine and spirits producers heading to ProWine Shanghai, the export-driven country is putting indigenous grapes and competitive pricing at the center of its pitch
takeaways: 23 Moldovan wine and spirits producers exhibit at ProWine Shanghai from November 10 to 12, seeking Chinese importers and distributors.
Moldova's wine imports to China reached US$1.43 million in the first nine months of 2026, per Chinese customs data.
About 85% of Moldovan wine production is exported, and the EU now takes roughly 60% of wine exports.

MARKET.head: Central Valley grower swaps wine grapes for almonds amid market and water pressures
MARKET.summ: After years of uncertainty in other crops, Proplant Transplanting is taking a measured approach to almonds
takeaways: Proplant Transplanting, a fourth-generation Central Valley family business, is replacing hundreds of acres of wine grapes with almonds.
Wine demand fell: US volume dropped about 4% from 2024 to 2025 and over 12% since 2018, per BMO.
Almond prices hit about $3.50 per pound in 2026, a decade high, though farming costs have also risen sharply.

MARKET.head: Australian wine's small formats gain ground as consumers seek moderation and convenience
MARKET.summ: Consumer demand for wine is changing globally, and while this has shown up in many mature markets as a decline in consumption, the shift in consumption habits has also uncovered an increasing consumer interest in smaller, more flexible packaging formats.
takeaways: Combined export and domestic off-trade sales of 187mL wine packs rose 22 per cent to almost 1.9 million litres in 2025-26.
Export volumes of 187mL packs grew 39 per cent, from 450,000 litres in 2023-24 to 620,000 litres in 2025-26.
Australia's single-person households reached 26 per cent of households, up from 18 per cent in 1981, per Census data.

MARKET.head: EU greenwashing rules now bind wine labels and sommelier talk on environmental claims
MARKET.summ: New restrictions on environmental marketing claims are putting terms like “natural” and “eco-friendly” under the microscope, prompting questions about what wineries can and can’t include on bottle labels
takeaways: Directive (EU) 2024/825, called EmpCo, restricts vague environmental claims like "eco-friendly" and "green" on products sold in the EU.
Enforcement began September 27, with fines up to four percent of annual turnover, set country by country by each member state.
Terms such as "natural" must be specified and substantiated, and old stock is not grandfathered in under the rules.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux takes 41% of weekly traded wine value on Liv-ex
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux strengthened its lead of the market, claiming 41% of traded value. Burgundy’s share also rose compared to last week
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value, with 2019 and 2020 vintages the top-traded by value.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany rose to 11.6%, per Liv-ex weekly trade data.

MARKET.head: India-EU trade deal to cut wine tariffs, but market entry remains complex
MARKET.summ: For years, India has occupied a peculiar position in the international wine industry: too large to ignore, too complicated to enter
takeaways: India's 150% tariff on EU wine will phase down to 20% for premium and 30% for medium-range wines under the India-EU FTA.
Alcohol is regulated state by state in India, so registration, taxation and distribution vary across markets.
India imported 5.4 million litres of wine worth US$28.8 million in 2025, up 13.7% in volume and 10.9% in value.

MARKET.head: California table grapes stay in supply through December despite early harvest
MARKET.summ: Despite an early start to harvest, steady shipments and cold storage supplies are in position to keep California table grapes available for holiday promotions
takeaways: California Table Grape Commission says harvest ends mid-November but shipments continue well into December.
Grape volumes will remain promotable through the holiday season, supported by steady shipments and cold storage supplies.
Consumer research cited shows 72% of grape purchasers prefer U.S.-grown grapes, versus under 5% preferring imports.

MARKET.head: Hong Kong-listed Grace Wine proposes renaming itself under 1919 founder's control
MARKET.summ: Hong Kong-listed Grace Wine Holdings has proposed changing its name as it expands beyond wine under the control of the founder of Chinese drinks retailer 1919
takeaways: Grace Wine Holdings proposed renaming itself Consumer Business Factory Holdings, referencing drinks retailer 1919, in an October 9 filing.
1919 founder Yang Lingjiang acquired a 73.63% controlling stake in Grace Wine in December 2025.
The company is expanding into sauce-aroma baijiu and supply-chain operations, moving away from its vertically integrated wine business.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads Liv-ex trade as Lynch-Bages 2005 becomes top-traded wine
MARKET.summ: US and UK buyers both upped their purchasing, the former segment reclaiming their share of purchasing
takeaways: Bordeaux held the lead on Liv-ex with a 37.4% share of purchases, and Lynch-Bages 2005 was the top-traded wine.
Burgundy's share fell to 15.4% from 18.4% last week, and was well below its 24.6% September average.
US buyers took over half of Bordeaux's purchased value, while US share of California trade rose to 9.6%.

CULTURE.head: Brendan Carter of Bottleshock named 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year
CULTURE.summ: Last night, Brendan Carter from Bottleshock was named the 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year by Wine Communicators of Australia (WCA). The announcement was the culmination of the celebrations at WCA’s sold out annual Awards Night in Sydney, with Brendan accepting his award from WCA National Chair, Lynda Schenk.
takeaways: Wine Communicators of Australia named Brendan Carter of Bottleshock its 2026 Wine Communicator of the Year at its Sydney Awards Night.
Judges assessed 33 entries across 13 categories, with WCA National Chair Lynda Schenk presenting the award to Carter.
Carter was recognised for his Bottleshock.TV content and The Big Blind League wine tasting competition, and urged Australian accents to lead global wine authority.

CULTURE.head: Stanley Wine Bar wins three awards at Tasmanian Wine List of the Year 2026
CULTURE.summ: Stanley Wine Bar has emerged as the standout of the 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards, taking home three major accolades, including the coveted Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List of the Year. The north-west coast gem also claimed Best Small Bar Wine List and, “proving the public agrees with the experts”,...
takeaways: Wine Tasmania's 2026 Tasmanian Wine List of the Year Awards honoured venues showcasing local Tasmanian wines.
Stanley Wine Bar, a north-west coast venue, won Overall Judges' Choice Best Tasmanian Wine List of the Year.
It also took Best Small Bar Wine List and the People's Choice Award, judged by a panel including Nola James.

CULTURE.head: Sommeliers name underrated Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc producers beyond famous regions
CULTURE.summ: Though it has centuries of history in Burgundy, great quality Pinot Noir can now be found in every corner of the world, from the volcanic Otago peninsula in New Zealand to the high plateaus of Greece’s Amyndeon region. Across these different areas, Pinot Noir offers a wide variety of expressions, from dense, fruit-forward...
takeaways: Sixteen sommeliers were asked to name the most underrated Pinot Noir on the market right now.
Picks include Redbank from King Valley, Australia, Wasenhaus from Baden, Germany, and Niedrist from Alto Adige, Italy.
A separate panel of ten sommeliers named underrated Sauvignon Blanc, including Casa Jipi from Baja, Mexico and Hannes Sabathi from Styria, Austria.

CULTURE.head: Napa consultant launches one-day Ask Wines chat with wine experts before Thanksgiving
CULTURE.summ: A new project empowers curious holiday drinkers to ask real experts for their advice
takeaways: Napa social media consultant Evan Roscoe launched Ask Wines, a 24-hour site answering Thanksgiving wine questions from human experts.
Roscoe recruited about 50 interested experts, including sommeliers, winemakers, wine buyers and drinks writers, via an Instagram poll.
The site runs the day before Thanksgiving, with questions expected on pairings, bottle quantities and grocery store choices.

CULTURE.head: Gippsland Wine Show awards 85 medals from 116 entries in record year
CULTURE.summ: In a record medal tally, the 2026 Farmer’s Daughters Gippsland Wine Show attracted 116 entries “with a strong focus on the region’s famed Pinot Noir and Chardonnay classes”. Wine Gippsland president Rob Lightfoot said there was an “outstanding haul” of 85 medals from the 103 varietal entries yielding seven trophies, “a...
takeaways: The 2026 Farmer's Daughters Gippsland Wine Show received 116 entries, with a strong focus on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay classes.
The show awarded 85 medals from 103 varietal entries, including 15 gold, 31 silver and 39 bronze, plus seven trophies.
Gippsland Wine Company's 2025 Loch Chardonnay, from South Gippsland, was named Best Wine of Show.

CULTURE.head: Alison Smith Story recounts her path into the wine business
CULTURE.summ: This episode of Wine 101 is brought to you by Wines of Alsace and Alsace Rocks. Tucked between the Vosges Mountains and the Rhine River in northeastern France, Alsace is one of the most distinctive wine regions on earth, and is home to centuries of family winemaking, some of France’s most certifiably organic vineyards, and a...
takeaways: Keith Beavers hosts this VinePair Wine 101 episode, which features Alison Smith Story of Smith Story Wines.
The conversation covers how Alison Smith Story came to work in the wine business, told casually.
The episode is sponsored by Wines of Alsace.

CULTURE.head: Volcanic soils make hard-to-farm vines and wines with a distinctive tension
CULTURE.summ:
Vines on volcanic soil are hard to grow and their grapes are hard-won, but it all combines to produce wines with a very particular sense of place

Good stories need jeopardy. Take The Princess Bride, one of my favourite films, which I recently introduced...
takeaways: Volcanic wines come from many soil types, including ash, basalt, obsidian, pumice and tuff, and vary widely in style.
Farming on volcanic terrain is difficult, as on La Palma, where growers face black ash soils, high winds and heatwaves.
Importer Nic Rizzi says volcanic wines carry an extra tension that reflects the hard conditions the vines grow in.

SCIENCE.head: Barossa workshop shows reworking old-vine Grenache takes patience, not haste
SCIENCE.summ: Last Thursday, a well-attended workshop discussing and demonstrating reworking old vine Grenache was held in the Barossa Valley. Hosted by The Barossa Viticulture Technical Group (BVTG) and led by technical viticulturist Tom Bartholomaeus as well as chief viticulturist Nigel Blieschke of Torbreck Vintners, the morning led...
takeaways: Torbreck viticulturists Nigel Blieschke and Tom Bartholomaeus led a Barossa Viticulture Technical Group workshop on reworking old-vine Grenache.
Block one, reworked in 2020, reached about 95% strike rate, while block two, reworked in 2022, reached only 75%.
Block two yielded about 1.3 tonnes per hectare less, as the team rushed the process and cordons and trunks grew weaker.

SCIENCE.head: 90% of Barossa vineyard area now in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia
SCIENCE.summ: Barossa Australia has revealed that more than 300 Barossa vineyards and wineries are now participating in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia, with over 80% achieving independent certification. 12,768 Ha (90%) of Barossa’s 14,162 Ha under-vine is participating in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia , a 1,264 hectare (10%) increase...
takeaways: Barossa Australia says 12,768 hectares, 90% of the region's 14,162 under-vine area, now participate in Sustainable Winegrowing Australia.
The program now has 303 Barossa vineyard and winery members, up 66% in two years, with 244 certified to best practice via Freshcare audit.
Government grants worth over $170,000 over five years have funded free certification training and expert viticulture sessions to lower program costs.

SCIENCE.head: Roller-crimped cover crops improve Mediterranean vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization
SCIENCE.summ: In a 2026 study published in Field Crops Research based on Mediterranean rainfed vineyards, the authors found that roller-crimping cover crops improved soil cover, vine water status, yield (in wetter conditions), and mycorrhizal colonization without affecting grape quality, while seasonal climate was the dominant driver of...
takeaways: A 2026 Field Crops Research study tested roller-crimped cover crops in Mediterranean rainfed vineyards.
Roller-crimping improved soil cover, vine water status and mycorrhizal colonization without changing grape quality.
Yield rose only in wetter seasons, while climate was the dominant driver of fungal diversity.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Images: Slice of Italy
NEWSLETTERS.summ: What else do you need really? A little farmhouse, a patch of grapes, some olive trees, and the rolling hills
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: A Vinography photo post shows a small Italian farmhouse set among grapevines, olive trees and rolling hills.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Bourgueil’s Aurélien Revillot
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Through a Burgundian lens, Cabernet Franc becomes a study of place and terroir, parcel by parcel
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Aurélien Revillot is a relative newcomer to the Bourgueil appellation whose domaine is part of Becky Wasserman's portfolio.
Revillot makes single-vineyard wines from his best slope parcels alongside an entry-level cuvée blended from several parcels.
At the time of the author's first visit in May 2022, Revillot had three finished cuvées, with two cuvées parcellaires due from the 2020 vintage.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Catalonia’s Under(wine)world
NEWSLETTERS.summ: How a Champagne trip in the 1800s resulted in a new Spanish wine in a league of its own
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Josep Raventós of Penedès produced Spain's first traditional method sparkling wine in 1872, using Spanish grapes rather than Champagne varieties.
Cava is produced mainly in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, Penedès, Catalonia, where 95% of Cava comes from, and its cellars can reach 20 m deep.
Sumarroca Gran Reserva Brut Nature Cava 2022 from Finca Sumarroca is aged 40 months and priced at $28 Cdn, per the author.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow visited Beijing, with a Guangzhou stop planned for November 6.
Spain ranked fifth for wine volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy but a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Entry-level picks highlighted include DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo, plus Verdejo from Ayuso and Campos Reales, priced around RMB12 to RMB24.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Why I Enjoy Wine Competition Judging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Plus a guide to Le Puy wines - my notes from a recent vertical tasting
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Columnist is judging at the Asia Wine Trophy in Daejeon, South Korea, the only competition known with a dedicated orange and amber wine panel.
A Georgian Khikhvi amber received mid-90s scores from all six judges and earned grand gold without discussion.
Le Puy, a biodynamic right-bank Bordeaux estate, left the Francs Côtes de Bordeaux appellation in 2017 and now bottles as Vin de France.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The 2026 Harvest Is In , Here’s What It’s Already Telling Us About this Burgundy Wine Vintage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Early harvest data from the 2026 Burgundy vintage reveals exciting insights into the region's grapes, offering a first look at vine yields and pricing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: Burgundy's Côte d'Or picking finished between 10 and 12 September, after the region's earliest harvest on record.
The Comité des Vins de Bourgogne estimates the 2026 crop is about 30 per cent below the five-year average, per early figures.
Growers report small, thick-skinned berries and healthy fruit, with Côte de Beaune acidity mostly holding up despite the heat.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Essential Kit for Kitchen Season
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Outfitting your kitchen with the season’s essential tools, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker says the clocks going back this Sunday marks the start of what she calls Kitchen Season.
During November and December, she says many people get a special urge to cook for others or try new cuisines.
Her article lists kitchen tools she uses year-round that become more essential during festive cooking.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family near O Grove, Galicia, ages its magnum Albariño underwater in the Galician estuary.
The Attis Albariño 'Mar' 2025 is aged five months under water at 13-16C, versus the 'Standard' bottling of about 120,000 bottles annually.
The author notes that past underwater-aged wines he tasted seemed older and less fresh than landbound counterparts.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude reviewed older vintage Port selections, dated 1985 to 2022, from an NYC media tasting that also featured the 2024 vintage.
The reviewer called the 2003 vintage Ports powerful, and said one 2003 bottle was probably his favorite of that vintage tasted so far.
Several selections were judged not yet ready, with the reviewer advising cellaring for roughly ten more years for the youngest wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Tannic Panic! Issue #148: Better Than Pinotage
NEWSLETTERS.summ: South African reds, including one $30 bottle rated 98 points by a prominent “wine critic”
NEWSLETTERS.author: Zach O'Brown
takeaways: Tannic Panic! tasted three South African Bordeaux-style blends, including a $35 bottle that Tim Atkin rated 98 points.
The reviewers scored the $35 Stellenbosch-area blend 92 points, calling it well balanced and a strong South African Cabernet blend.
One blend scored 80 points and was called sour with a short finish, dominated by Cabernet Franc's smoky, green notes.
